original_value: Integrating deep learning with latent state space models has the potential to yield temporal models that are powerful, yet tractable and interpretable. Unfortunately, current models are not designed to handle missing data or multiple data modalities, which are both prevalent in real-world data. In this work, we introduce a factorized inference method for Multimodal Deep Markov Models (MDMMs), allowing us to filter and smooth in the presence of missing data, while also performing uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion. We derive this method by factorizing the posterior p(z|x) for non-linear state space models, and develop a variational backward-forward algorithm for inference. Because our method handles incompleteness over both time and modalities, it is capable of interpolation, extrapolation, conditional generation, label prediction, and weakly supervised learning of multimodal time series. We demonstrate these capabilities on both synthetic and real-world multimodal data under high levels of data deletion. Our method performs well even with more than 50% missing data, and outperforms existing deep approaches to inference in latent time series.

result.paraphrase: Integrating deep learning with latent state-space models can produce temporal models that are both powerful and tractable, with interpretable behavior. However, existing models are not built to cope with missing data or multiple data modalities, two traits commonly found in real-world datasets. Here, we present a factorized inference approach for Multimodal Deep Markov Models (MDMMs) that enables filtering and smoothing despite missing values, while also carrying out uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion. The method is derived by factorizing the posterior p(z|x) for nonlinear state-space models, and we devise a variational backward-forward inference algorithm. By addressing incompleteness across both time and modalities, it supports interpolation, extrapolation, conditional generation, label prediction, and weakly supervised learning for multimodal time series. We show these abilities on synthetic and real-world multimodal data with severe data deletion. Even with over 50% missing data, the method performs strongly and exceeds existing deep inference approaches for latent time series.
